bullets.title: Jensen Huang teases undisclosed 'surprising new product' at Nvidia
bullets.body: Jensen Huang publicly stated "we have a surprising new product that we haven't told anyone about," with sell-side research separately flagging that Nvidia is testing GPU-to-GPU hybrid bonding technology, with the N1/N1X identified as the most likely candidate.

bullets.title: AI optical supply chain firing on all cylinders: LITE sold out, COHR backlog to CY28, MRVL interconnect +70%
bullets.body: Three May earnings reports across the AI optical stack told a consistent demand story: LITE reported lasers sold out, COHR reported a record backlog extending to calendar year 2028, and MRVL raised its interconnect growth outlook from +50% to +70%. Commentary affirms "optics is the future of data center" connectivity.

bullets.title: Intel betting billions on EMIB packaging as cost-competitive 2.5D alternative to TSMC
bullets.body: Per Korean media reports, Intel is investing several billion dollars in EMIB advanced packaging, said to offer better cost and productivity than TSMC-led silicon interposer-based 2.5D. Intel is also planning large-scale adoption of silicon capacitors in AI chips starting next year, with EMIB growing rapidly as the cornerstone of its foundry revival.

bullets.title: Chip stocks racing toward biggest gains since Dotcom era on AI demand — FT
bullets.body: The Financial Times notes semiconductor stocks are approaching their largest gains since the Dotcom boom, driven by surging AI infrastructure demand, with names like NVDA, AMD, MRVL, and TSM cited in the momentum.

bullets.title: NBIS becomes Leopold's single largest position at ~20% of portfolio
bullets.body: Leopold has reportedly made NBIS his top holding at approximately 20% of his portfolio, exceeding SNDK and running at roughly 3x his BE allocation. The disclosure has drawn fintwit attention given the concentrated sizing.

bullets.title: IONQ commands revenue scale and backlog that INFQ valuation parity doesn't reflect
bullets.body: A fintwit account argues IONQ should trade at a premium to INFQ despite matching forward P/S multiples: IONQ generates $64.7M/quarter vs. INFQ's $9.5M and carries a $470M contract backlog. The poster sees an attractive entry point in quantum stocks as the technology becomes more tangible.

bullets.title: IREN customer Fireworks AI surpasses $800M ARR ahead of B300 GPU deployment
bullets.body: Fireworks AI, an IREN customer, has surpassed $800M ARR, with B300 GPU deployment expected soon across Childress and other IREN locations — signaling healthy demand at the hyperscale customer level.

bullets.title: META tests AI subscriptions and new paid tiers for Facebook and Instagram
bullets.body: META is piloting AI subscription products and rolling out new paid plans across Facebook and Instagram, representing an early-stage monetization push on its AI investments.

bullets.title: Geopolitical flare-up: U.S.-Iran strikes drive futures and bonds lower, oil surges
bullets.body: Resumed U.S. military strikes on Iran and Iran's condemnation of ceasefire violations sent European equity futures down (EuroStoxx 50 -1.2%, FTSE -0.95%, DAX -0.93%), bonds lower, and oil sharply higher. ECB separately warned that markets are underestimating geopolitical and fiscal risks.

bullets.title: Core PCE inflation expected to tick up in April, reinforcing Fed hawkish lean
bullets.body: Pre-release consensus points to a higher April core PCE print, which would reinforce the Fed's hawkish tilt and keep rate-cut expectations under pressure.

bullets.title: SpaceX-Anthropic Colossus lease: 180-day term with 90-day mutual exit, SpaceX's choice
bullets.body: Elon Musk clarified SpaceX has made no long-term commitment to lease Colossus; the current structure is a 180-day lease with a 90-day mutual cancellation clause, and the short duration was SpaceX's preference — not Anthropic's.

bullets.title: Huawei Kirin potentially integrating MEMS micropumps for chip thermal management
bullets.body: Fintwit flagged speculation that Huawei may be embedding MEMS micropumps into its Kirin chip for cooling, which would represent a significant thermal management breakthrough and further evidence of Huawei's chip self-sufficiency push.

bullets.title: MLCC price hike cycle may be starting: Murata, Samsung EM signal increases, Yageo follows
bullets.body: World's #1 and #2 MLCC makers — Murata and Samsung Electro-Mechanics — have issued price increase notices, with Yageo officially acknowledging the signals. This may indicate the start of a passive component pricing upcycle relevant to the broader semiconductor supply chain.
